title: Psalms Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 6.

questions.question: In Psalms 6, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: O LORD, rebuke me not in thine anger
Have mercy upon me, O LORD
Return, O LORD, deliver my soul
My soul is also sore vexed
questions.correctAnswer: O LORD, rebuke me not in thine anger
questions.explanation: This phrase is found in Psalms 6:1, making it the first statement in the chapter.

questions.question: What does David ask the LORD not to do in His anger?
questions.explanation: This is stated in Psalms 6:1 where David specifically asks the LORD not to rebuke him.

questions.question: What does David request from the LORD due to his weakness?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 6:2, David directly asks the LORD for mercy because he is weak.

questions.question: According to David, what is vexed?
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:2 mentions that David's bones are vexed.

questions.question: In Psalms 6, what does David ask the LORD to heal?
questions.explanation: This request is found in Psalms 6:2 where David asks the LORD to heal his bones.

questions.question: What is David's soul described as in Psalms 6:3?
questions.explanation: David describes his soul as sore vexed in Psalms 6:3.

questions.question: What does David ask the LORD about the duration of his suffering?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 6:3, David asks the LORD, 'but thou, O LORD, how long?'

questions.question: What does David implore the LORD to do for his soul?
questions.explanation: This appeal is made in Psalms 6:4 where David asks the LORD to deliver his soul.

questions.question: For what reason does David ask to be saved?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 6:4, David specifies that he asks to be saved for the sake of the LORD's mercies.

questions.question: What does David express about his condition in Psalms 6?
questions.explanation: David states in Psalms 6:2 that he is weak and asks for mercy.

questions.question: David mentions which aspect of his physical state in Psalms 6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:2 specifically mentions that David's bones are vexed.

questions.question: Is it true that David feels he is being chastened in anger?
questions.explanation: David asks the LORD not to chasten him in His hot displeasure, indicating he feels he is being chastened.

questions.question: Is it true that David desires mercy from the LORD?
questions.explanation: David explicitly asks for mercy from the LORD in Psalms 6:2.

questions.question: Is it false that David asks the LORD to heal him because he is joyful?
questions.explanation: David asks the LORD to heal him because he is weak, not joyful, as stated in Psalms 6:2.

questions.question: Is it false that David claims he has no troubles in Psalms 6?
questions.explanation: David expresses that he is sore vexed and asks for help, indicating he has troubles, as seen in Psalms 6:3.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 6:5, what is true about death in relation to remembering the Lord?
options: In death there is no remembrance of thee
In death the Lord is praised
Death brings eternal thanks to God
The grave is full of songs of praise
questions.correctAnswer: In death there is no remembrance of thee
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:5 states 'For in death there is no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?' indicating that death ends remembrance of the Lord.

questions.question: What does Psalms 6:8 promise will happen if someone is a worker of iniquity as commanded in Psalms 6:7?
options: The LORD hath heard the voice of my weeping
They will be comforted by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD hath heard the voice of my weeping
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:7 says the eye waxeth old because of enemies, and Psalms 6:8 commands workers of iniquity to depart because the LORD has heard the voice of the psalmist's weeping, showing God listens to the afflicted.

questions.question: What physical condition does the psalmist describe in Psalms 6:6 as a result of his grief?
options: He waters his couch with tears
questions.correctAnswer: He waters his couch with tears
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:6 says 'I water my couch with my tears,' describing his sorrow physically affecting his rest.

questions.question: How do Psalms 6:5 and Psalms 6:8 relate to each other in terms of God’s response to the psalmist’s condition?
options: Though death ends praise, God hears the living's weeping
God forgets the living but remembers the dead
The grave is a place of praise, and God ignores the living
questions.correctAnswer: Though death ends praise, God hears the living's weeping
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:5 notes no remembrance of God in death, while 6:8 confirms God hears the psalmist’s weeping, emphasizing God's attention to the living’s prayers.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask the LORD not to do in Psalms 6:1?
options: Rebuke me not in thine anger
questions.correctAnswer: Rebuke me not in thine anger
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:1 says 'O LORD, rebuke me not in thine anger,' showing a plea for mercy rather than harsh judgment.

questions.question: Why does the psalmist say his bones are vexed in Psalms 6:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:2 states 'Have mercy upon me, O LORD; for I am weak: O LORD, heal me; for my bones are vexed,' linking his physical distress to weakness.

questions.question: What emotional state is expressed in Psalms 6:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:3 says 'My soul is also sore vexed,' indicating deep emotional distress.

questions.question: What does the psalmist request from the LORD in Psalms 6:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:4 states 'Return, O LORD, deliver my soul: oh save me for thy mercies' sake,' showing a plea for rescue based on God's mercy.

questions.question: What does the psalmist say about his eye in Psalms 6:7?
options: It is consumed because of grief
questions.correctAnswer: It is consumed because of grief
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:7 says 'Mine eye is consumed because of grief,' indicating that sorrow has exhausted him physically.

questions.question: What instruction does the psalmist give to workers of iniquity in Psalms 6:8?
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:8 commands 'Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity,' showing separation from evildoers.

questions.question: How does the psalmist describe the effect of his groaning on his body in Psalms 6:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:6 states 'I am weary with my groaning,' showing the physical toll of his sorrow.

questions.question: What does the psalmist imply about God’s awareness of his suffering in Psalms 6:8?
options: The LORD hath heard the voice of my weeping
God is unaware of my pain
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD hath heard the voice of my weeping
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:8 affirms that God hears the psalmist’s sorrowful cries, giving hope amid distress.

questions.question: The psalmist’s request for mercy in Psalms 6:2 shows a recognition of what human condition?
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:2 directly states 'for I am weak,' highlighting human frailty and need for divine mercy.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist believes that even in death, people can give thanks to God according to Psalms 6:5.
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:5 declares 'in death there is no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?' denying praise in death.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 6:4, the psalmist asks God to deliver his soul and save him for His mercies' sake.
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:4 states 'Return, O LORD, deliver my soul: oh save me for thy mercies' sake,' confirming this prayer.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 6.

questions.question: What has the LORD done regarding David's supplication?
options: The LORD hath heard my supplication
The LORD hath forgotten my supplication
The LORD hath ignored my supplication
The LORD hath rejected my supplication
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD hath heard my supplication
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Psalms 6:9 explicitly states, 'The LORD hath heard my supplication; the LORD will receive my prayer.'

questions.question: What does David express about his enemies in Psalms 6:10?
options: Let them return and be ashamed suddenly
questions.correctAnswer: Let them return and be ashamed suddenly
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:10 states, 'Let all mine enemies be ashamed and sore vexed: let them return and be ashamed suddenly.'

questions.question: According to David in Psalms 6:4, what does he ask the LORD for?
questions.explanation: David pleads for deliverance when he says, 'Return, O LORD, deliver my soul: oh save me for thy mercies' sake.' (Psalms 6:4)

questions.question: What does David mean by 'my bones are vexed' in Psalms 6:2?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 6:2, David expresses physical and emotional distress, saying, 'for I am weak: O LORD, heal me; for my bones are vexed.'

questions.question: What emotion does David express in Psalms 6:6?
questions.explanation: David describes his sorrow and weeping in Psalms 6:6, stating, 'I water my couch with my tears.'

questions.question: In Psalms 6:8, what does David ask the workers of iniquity to do?
questions.explanation: David calls for separation from evil in Psalms 6:8: 'Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity; for the LORD hath heard the voice of my weeping.'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'supplication' in Psalms 6:9 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'supplication' implies a heartfelt request or cry for help, aligning with David's plea in Psalms 6:9.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Psalms 6:10 with the phrase 'let them return and be ashamed suddenly'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:10 employs parallelism, where the two phrases mirror each other in structure and meaning.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of God hearing prayers as seen in Psalms 6:9?
questions.explanation: 1 John 5:14 states, 'And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us,' echoing the theme from Psalms 6:9.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage reflects the concept of shame for enemies as in Psalms 6:10?
questions.explanation: Psalm 35:4 says, 'Let them be confounded and put to shame that seek after my soul,' reflecting the same theme of shame for enemies found in Psalms 6:10.

questions.question: What comes immediately before David's plea for mercy in Psalms 6:2?
options: O LORD, rebuke me not in thine anger
questions.correctAnswer: O LORD, rebuke me not in thine anger
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:1 precedes David's plea in verse 2 with a cry for the LORD not to rebuke him in anger.

questions.question: What follows immediately after David's expression of grief in Psalms 6:7?
options: Let all mine enemies be ashamed
For in death there is no remembrance of thee
questions.correctAnswer: Let all mine enemies be ashamed
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:8 follows David's expression of grief with a declaration about his enemies: 'Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.'

questions.question: David's lament in Psalms 6 is a reflection of his what?
questions.explanation: Psalms 6 reflects David's deep suffering and plea for mercy, particularly seen in verses like Psalms 6:2 and 6:3.

questions.question: David's assurance in Psalms 6:9 indicates what about his relationship with God?
questions.explanation: David's assurance that 'the LORD hath heard my supplication' in Psalms 6:9 indicates a trusting relationship with God.

questions.question: The phrase 'let them return and be ashamed suddenly' suggests a gradual process of shame.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'let them return and be ashamed suddenly' in Psalms 6:10 indicates an immediate action rather than a gradual process.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 6:1 teach about God's nature in relation to human sin?
options: God's anger is a righteous response to sin requiring repentance
God ignores human sin out of sheer mercy
God is indifferent to human disobedience
God punishes without opportunity for repentance
questions.correctAnswer: God's anger is a righteous response to sin requiring repentance
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:1 says, 'O LORD, rebuke me not in thine anger, neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure,' indicating that God's anger is a just and disciplinary response to sin, not arbitrary or indifferent.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human weakness and divine healing does Psalms 6:2 teach?
options: Human frailty necessitates divine mercy and healing
Humans are inherently strong and do not require God's healing
Healing is only physical and unrelated to spiritual condition
Divine healing is guaranteed regardless of human condition
questions.correctAnswer: Human frailty necessitates divine mercy and healing
questions.explanation: The psalmist pleads, 'Have mercy upon me, O LORD; for I am weak: O LORD, heal me; for my bones are vexed' (Psalms 6:2), acknowledging human weakness and dependence on God's mercy and healing.

questions.question: What doctrine about the soul's experience of suffering and hope is taught in Psalms 6:3?
options: The soul experiences deep anguish but continues to hope in God's timing
The soul is unaffected by suffering
Suffering is a sign of God's rejection with no hope
The soul should ignore suffering to maintain faith
questions.correctAnswer: The soul experiences deep anguish but continues to hope in God's timing
questions.explanation: Verse 3 states, 'My soul is also sore vexed: but thou, O LORD, how long?' showing the psalmist's anguish yet persistent hope in God's deliverance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 6:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks, 'Return, O LORD, deliver my soul: oh save me for thy mercies' sake' (Psalms 6:4), highlighting God's attribute of mercy towards sinners.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified in Psalms 6:5 concerning God's relationship to death and remembrance?
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:5 states, 'For in death there is no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?' This reflects God's sovereign control over life and death and the finality of death apart from Him.

questions.question: How does Psalms 6 prepare for the New Testament theme of Jesus' intercessory suffering?
options: By illustrating the believer's plea for mercy and healing amid suffering
By denying any need for intercession
By focusing solely on physical healing without spiritual significance
By emphasizing human self-sufficiency in overcoming sin
questions.correctAnswer: By illustrating the believer's plea for mercy and healing amid suffering
questions.explanation: The psalm’s lament and plea for deliverance (e.g., Psalms 6:2-4) typify the believer’s dependence on divine mercy, prefiguring Christ’s intercessory role as seen in Hebrews 7:25.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Psalms 6:6-7 connect to in Scripture?
options: The theme of lament as a form of sanctification and perseverance
The theme of immediate triumph over enemies
The denial of grief in the life of the believer
The notion that suffering is irrelevant to faith
questions.correctAnswer: The theme of lament as a form of sanctification and perseverance
questions.explanation: Verses 6-7 describe deep grief and tears, connecting to the biblical motif of lament (e.g., in Lamentations) which functions in sanctification by fostering dependence on God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 6:8 and Psalms 6:9 teach about God's attentiveness to prayer and justice?
options: God hears the cries of the righteous and acts justly against the wicked
God is indifferent to human suffering and does not hear prayers
God hears but does not act on prayers
God is only concerned with communal prayers, not individual ones
questions.correctAnswer: God hears the cries of the righteous and acts justly against the wicked
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says, 'the LORD hath heard the voice of my weeping,' and verse 9 confirms, 'The LORD hath heard my supplication; the LORD will receive my prayer,' showing God's justice and attentiveness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about the fate of the wicked is taught in Psalms 6:8 and Psalms 6:10?
options: The wicked will be separated from the righteous and experience shame
The wicked will ultimately triumph over the righteous
The wicked are forgiven unconditionally without repentance
The wicked are ignored by God and left unpunished
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked will be separated from the righteous and experience shame
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:8 commands 'Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity,' while verse 10 says, 'Let all mine enemies be ashamed and sore vexed,' indicating divine judgment and separation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine concerning human sorrow and divine comfort is taught in Psalms 6:6 and Psalms 6:4?
options: Human sorrow invites divine deliverance and comfort through mercy
Human sorrow is irrelevant to God's actions
Divine comfort is unrelated to human lament
God rejects those who express sorrow
questions.correctAnswer: Human sorrow invites divine deliverance and comfort through mercy
questions.explanation: Verse 6 depicts sorrow ('I water my couch with my tears'), while verse 4 pleads for deliverance 'for thy mercies' sake,' showing sorrow as the context for divine comfort.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that Psalms 6:1-10 reveals a capricious God who punishes without cause. What does Psalms 6:1-10 actually teach?
options: God's discipline is just and merciful, aimed at repentance and restoration
God punishes arbitrarily without regard to human behavior
God abandons the penitent in their suffering
God's anger is permanent and unchangeable
questions.correctAnswer: God's discipline is just and merciful, aimed at repentance and restoration
questions.explanation: The psalmist requests mercy and healing (Psalms 6:1-2), acknowledges God's anger as disciplinary (6:1), and trusts in God’s hearing and deliverance (6:8-9), showing a just and merciful God.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification and perseverance is taught in Psalms 6:7 and Psalms 6:10?
options: God sustains the believer in affliction and ultimately vindicates him over enemies
The believer is left to suffer without hope for vindication
Sanctification is immediate and without struggle
questions.correctAnswer: God sustains the believer in affliction and ultimately vindicates him over enemies
questions.explanation: Verse 7 notes the psalmist’s grief from enemies, while verse 10 prays for their shame, reflecting God’s sustaining presence and ultimate vindication.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Psalms 6:9 that reveals God's response to prayer?
questions.explanation: Psalms 6:9 states, 'The LORD hath heard my supplication; the LORD will receive my prayer,' demonstrating God's faithfulness in hearing and answering prayer.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about human mortality and eternal consequence is taught in Psalms 6:5?
options: Death is final and separates one from the opportunity to praise God
Death enhances human ability to worship God
There is no consequence to death in relation to God
The grave is a place of ongoing worship
questions.correctAnswer: Death is final and separates one from the opportunity to praise God
questions.explanation: Verse 5 states, 'For in death there is no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?' highlighting the finality of death regarding worship.

questions.question: How does Psalms 6:3 and Psalms 6:6 together express the theological reality of spiritual and physical suffering?
options: Both soul and body suffer deeply, evidencing holistic human distress needing divine intervention
Only the body suffers; the soul remains unaffected
Suffering is purely spiritual with no bodily impact
questions.correctAnswer: Both soul and body suffer deeply, evidencing holistic human distress needing divine intervention
questions.explanation: Verse 3 shows the soul is sore vexed, and verse 6 describes physical weeping and sorrow, together illustrating total human distress.
